investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state within the eval window.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes advertise the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but have no remaining allocatable capacity (0/2 nodes had sufficient vm slots). The other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 128–152 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out, producing empty evidence objects and failing all contract assertions. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool in the production-api Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state within the eval window.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes advertise the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but have no remaining allocatable capacity (0/2 nodes had sufficient vm slots). The other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 128–152 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out, producing empty evidence objects and failing all contract assertions. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool in the production-api Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or cluster tooling shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is not exhausted on the two eligible nodes (i.e., available slots > 0 at the time of the eval run), the resource-exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened.

If the remote-agent pod spec's node affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude more nodes (reducing the eligible pool below 2), the primary cause would shift to a configuration change rather than resource exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly held lock or a just-released VM slot) rather than sustained exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-state failed while remote-agent-create or remote-agent-runtime passed in the same run window, the cause would be isolated to the state-polling logic rather than the shared scheduling layer.

If the two kata-eligible nodes show ample VM capacity but the peer-pod daemon or cloud VM quota is the bottleneck, the root cause would be at the provider layer rather than the Kubernetes resource accounting layer.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod created by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." The remote agent VM pod could not be placed on any node, so the agent never started, no runtime response was produced, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) remained absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent VM provisioning has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. Of the remaining 4 nodes, none match the pod's node affinity or selector requirements. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 kata-capable nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck unscheduled for 128–152 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence payload and a contract validation failure for all five required fields. The root cause is a resource exhaustion condition on the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or the expected-output contract.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 kata-capable nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported by the identical scheduler message across all three sibling checks within a ~5-minute window.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, which could indicate a labeling change or a misconfigured node selector on the remote agent pod spec. This is a contributing constraint but not the primary blocker since the 2 kata nodes are reachable but full.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, and their combined VM capacity is insufficient to absorb concurrent eval-created agents plus any existing workloads. No preemption victims exist, suggesting all slots are held by non-preemptible pods.

Lower probability — transient burst of concurrent remote agent workloads from other sources temporarily exhausted the pool at the time of the eval run. This would be self-resolving and would not explain a sustained failure across three sequential checks spanning ~5 minutes.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Verifies whether the 4 non-kata nodes have always lacked the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource or whether a recent label/taint change caused them to stop matching the remote agent pod's node affinity selector.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes show available (unallocated) VM slots at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., node affinity misconfiguration or admission webhook rejection) must be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds and produces all five required evidence fields, the failure was a transient capacity burst rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.

If the 4 non-kata nodes are found to have been recently relabeled or had their node selectors changed such that they previously matched the remote agent pod spec, the affinity mismatch would be a regression rather than a static constraint.

If the remote-agent pod spec itself was recently changed to request more kata.peerpods.io/vm units per pod (e.g., from 1 to 2), that would reduce effective capacity and could explain exhaustion even without a cluster-level change.
If local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) are also failing with scheduling errors, the problem may be broader than the kata node pool.

Add an eval that monitors the count of Pending remote agent pods older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 60s) to detect scheduling backlogs before they cause full eval timeouts.

Add a node-pool-health check eval that verifies at least N kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available across the cluster, providing an early warning before the remote-agent-create/state/runtime checks begin to fail.

Consider a canary eval that runs remote-agent-create with a short timeout specifically to detect scheduling failures quickly, separate from the full runtime round-trip eval, so the signal is faster and more targeted.
